definitions.explanation: A spouse's parent — either the father-in-law or mother-in-law.
A parent who is not biologically related but has a parental role through remarriage.

examples.japanese: {義理|ぎり}の{親|おや}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{挨拶|あいさつ}した→挨拶する：01797_aisatsusuru⟧。
{義理|ぎり}の{親|おや}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{関係|かんけい}→関係：01298_kankei⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{悩|なや}んでいる→悩む：02380_nayamu⟧。
examples.english: I'm struggling with my relationship with my in-laws.

examples.japanese: ⟦{正月|しょうがつ}→正月：01433_shougatsu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{義理|ぎり}の{親|おや}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{家|いえ}→家：00612_ie⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{行|い}く→行く：00119_iku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{緊張|きんちょう}する→緊張する：20557_kinchousuru⟧。
examples.english: Going to my in-laws' house for New Year's makes me nervous.
I get along well with my stepparent.

examples.japanese: ⟦{母|はは}→母：00549_haha⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{再婚|さいこん}して→再婚する：25476_saikonsuru⟧、{義理|ぎり}の{親|おや}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦できた→できる：00557_dekiru⟧。
examples.english: My mother remarried, and I got a stepparent.

examples.japanese: {義理|ぎり}の{親|おや}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{本当|ほんとう}→本当：00779_hontou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{親|おや}→親：01357_oya⟧⟦のように→のように：30291_noyouni⟧⟦{慕|した}っている→慕う：09912_shitau⟧。
examples.english: I look up to my stepparent as if they were my real parent.

notes:
FORMS:
⟦{義理|ぎり}→義理：10891_giri⟧ (duty, obligation; in-law) + ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧ (possessive) + ⟦{親|おや}→親：01357_oya⟧ (parent)

The ⟦{義理|ぎり}→義理：10891_giri⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧～ pattern is used to form many in-law and step-family terms:
- ⟦{義理|ぎり}の{父|ちち}→義理の父：17117_girinochichi⟧: father-in-law / stepfather
- ⟦{義理|ぎり}→義理：10891_giri⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{母|はは}→母：00549_haha⟧: mother-in-law / stepmother
- ⟦{義理|ぎり}→義理：10891_giri⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{兄弟|きょうだい}→兄弟：00964_kyoudai⟧: siblings-in-law / stepsiblings
- ⟦{義理|ぎり}→義理：10891_giri⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{息子|むすこ}→息子：00799_musuko⟧: son-in-law
- ⟦{義理|ぎり}→義理：10891_giri⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{娘|むすめ}→娘：02263_musume⟧: daughter-in-law

FORMAL EQUIVALENTS:
- ⟦{義父|ぎふ}→義父：06725_gifu⟧: father-in-law (formal)
- ⟦{義母|ぎぼ}→義母：06724_gibo⟧: mother-in-law (formal)
- {義両親|ぎりょうしん}: parents-in-law (formal)

CULTURAL NOTE:
Relationships with {義理|ぎり}の{親|おや} are a frequent topic in Japanese advice columns and online forums, especially regarding expectations during holidays and family gatherings.
